blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 5 killings of trans and gender-identity-diverse people in 2025, matching the mid-band of the comparison states/provinces. Against a population of about 8.7 million the rate is approximately 0.57 per million per year, above the national rate of 0.38 per million. This state/province spans the vast equatorial rainforest basin, where the finding that 68% of killings occur outside state/provincial capitals means interior municipal exposure is difficult to assess and infrastructure for protection is thinner.

The above-national rate and geographic risk-concentration place this state/province modestly below the national norm. Against a neighbouring coastal state, which had 8 killings on a population of about 9 million (a rate of about 0.89 per million), this state/province is less severe on a per-capita basis, but the rainforest-interior geography amplifies the difficulty of accessing help after an incident for a visitor. No unit-specific legal or ordinance finding was identified.
